text.p: These are the leading stories in the Belgrade press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified them and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Yugoslavia's full return to the world is in Hungary's interests, Hungarian president Arpad Goncz says in talks with Yugoslav defence minister Pavle Bulatovic.
- Yugoslav railways and French firm Valdunes sign deal for joint production of wagon wheels and axles whose value will reach around 80 million French francs in the next five years.
- Proposed law on Serbian pensions, which comes into effect on January 1, 1997, abolishes early retirement and second category of disability benefits.
- Pre-election silence begins at midnight on Thursday before the November 3 federal elections.
- New digital telephone switchboard opened in main Belgrade post office, expanding its capacity by 20,000 telephone lines. Equipment supplied by Alcatel-EI joint venture firm.
- Democracy is the oldest and deepest characteristic of the left, said Yugoslav United Left (JUL) leader Mira Markovic during the party's final pre-election presentation.

- Belgrade-Sarajevo bus traffic to be normalised by the end of next week, no more visa or vehicle insurance fees will be required for entry into Yugoslavia, says Belgrade bus company Lasta director Zoran Leontijevic.
- Police patrols stepped up in Yugoslav capital for three major events -- opposition coalition Zajedno and Serbian Radical Party campaign rallies and Red Star-Barcelona soccer match.

- Momir Bulatovic, president of Montenegro and Democratic Party of Socialists, says opposition leaders will face trial after elections for accusations against Montenegrin leadership during election campaigning.
- Arrival of foreign observers for federal elections in Yugoslavia still uncertain. Invitations sent out too late. U.S. observers at Montenegro elections.
- Settlement of Kosovo's status will have crucial influence on Yugoslavia's return to both political and financial international institutions, western diplomats in Belgrade say.
- Head of Kosovo Human Rights Committee Adem Demaci calls for international conference on Kosovo.
- More than 30,000 Yugoslavs rely on soup kitchens, says Morris O'Neil, head of soup kitchen programme in Yugoslavia. -- Belgrade newsroom +381 11 2224305
